title: file_specialist_map.csv can never produce a primary_specialist == S02 row -- S02 has zero primary-owned files by tool construction
claim: _analysis/tools/build_specialist_map.py's COMPONENT dict maps top_component "home-mixer" to ["S01"] as the first (and therefore primary_specialist, via `passes[0]`) entry unconditionally (L14). S02 is appended later, conditionally, only for rows where D07/D08 is in the file's domains or the path starts with `home-mixer/selectors/` or `home-mixer/ads/` (L34-36) -- but appended entries never become `passes[0]`. Because no top_component in the COMPONENT dict maps to S02 as its first entry, and S02 is only ever reachable through this home-mixer-only conditional append, `primary_specialist == "S02"` is mathematically impossible for any row in the generated CSV. A direct query confirms this: `awk -F',' 'NR>1 && $4=="S02"' file_specialist_map.csv` returns zero rows, while `awk -F',' 'NR>1 && $3 ~ /S02/' file_specialist_map.csv` returns exactly 62 rows, all with primary_specialist=="S01". The same structural gap applies to S06, S17, and S18 (none appear as primary_specialist for any row either), though only S02's absence was in scope for this pass.

runtime_caveats: This is a property of the mapping tool's generated output, not of the underlying source repository -- it says nothing about whether Home Mixer's filters/selectors/ads/frames are behaviorally important (they are; see the rest of this report).

This pass substituted the 62 rows where specialist_passes contains "S02" as the operational working set, documented explicitly throughout this pass's artifacts and never conflated with 'primary_specialist==S02'.

title: BlenderSelector's insertion call order makes a pinned Push-to-Home post displace already-placed Prompts and Who-to-Follow content to lower positions
claim: BlenderSelector::select (home-mixer/selectors/blender_selector.rs L65-71) calls, in this exact order: `blender.blend(posts, ads)`, then `insert_prompts`, then `insert_who_to_follow`, then `pin_push_to_home`, then `insert_frames`, then `insert_feed_survey`. `insert_prompts` inserts each prompt at increasing indices starting at 0 (stacking prompts at the very front of the list-so-far). `insert_who_to_follow` inserts the WTF module at `min(WHO_TO_FOLLOW_POSITION-1, len)` = index 5 (WHO_TO_FOLLOW_POSITION=6 per home-mixer/params/config.rs L29). `pin_push_to_home` runs *after* both of these and unconditionally inserts at literal index 0 (L127-133), so whenever a push-to-home post is present it ends up strictly ahead of any already-placed prompts and the WTF module, shifting their effective final position down by exactly one slot each relative to what their own insertion logic computed in isolation.

verification_evidence.symbol_or_section: BlenderSelector::select's insertion call sequence; insert_prompts; insert_who_to_follow; pin_push_to_home
WHO_TO_FOLLOW_POSITION=6, PROMPTS_POSITION=0, FEED_SURVEY_POSITION=12

runtime_caveats: PushToHomeSource only enables when query.push_to_home_post_id is set (a deep-link/push-notification-triggered request), so this interaction is rare in practice, not a general-request phenomenon.

Not evaluated as a bug -- pinning push-to-home content literally first is plausibly the intended product behavior for a 'you tapped a notification, here's that post' flow; flagged because the mechanism (call-order-dependent absolute-index insertion, not an explicit priority field) is non-obvious from reading any single function in isolation.
notes: Each of insert_prompts/insert_who_to_follow/pin_push_to_home/insert_frames/insert_feed_survey computes its insertion index independently against the list state at the moment it runs, not against a shared priority/slot model -- so the final composition order is an artifact of the fixed call sequence in BlenderSelector::select, not a documented priority table anywhere in this snapshot.

title: BlenderSelector never renumbers FeedItem.position after inserting non-post content, leaving organic post/ad position fields stale relative to final list order
claim: Each AdsBlender's blend_impl (partition_organic_blender.rs L194-196, safe_gap via interleave_and_finalize L209-211, time_gap_blender.rs L172-174, following_ad_blender.rs L184-186) ends with a loop that reassigns `item.position = i as i32` for every item 0..N -- so the post+ad list returned to BlenderSelector::select has internally-consistent sequential positions. However, BlenderSelector::select (home-mixer/selectors/blender_selector.rs L65-90) never performs an equivalent renumbering pass after insert_prompts/insert_who_to_follow/pin_push_to_home/insert_frames/insert_feed_survey shift every later item's true list index. The organic posts' and ads' `.position` fields therefore reflect their index within the smaller post+ad-only blend, not their final index in the returned `selected: Vec<FeedItem>`. Separately, insert_prompts assigns every prompt `position: PROMPTS_POSITION` (=0, a constant) regardless of its actual insertion index, so multiple prompts in one response all report the same `.position` value.

verification_evidence.symbol_or_section: select() body (no renumbering pass); insert_prompts (fixed PROMPTS_POSITION per item)
final renumbering loop inside blend_impl, before returning to the caller
build_entries called with `position` derived from `items.iter().enumerate()` over the actual selected_candidates list, not from `item.position`

Whether the client-facing URT/protobuf marshalling layer (home-mixer/util/urt/*, S01-primary, not independently opened in this pass) reads `.position` verbatim or also re-derives it from list order was not established -- this is the material unresolved consequence, hence STRONG_INFERENCE/PARTIALLY_CONFIRMED rather than DIRECT/CONFIRMED for any user-visible effect.
notes: Routed onward: whoever opens home-mixer/util/urt/post_marshaller.rs and sibling marshallers next should check whether `FeedItem.position` is trusted or ignored in favor of response-array order.

title: AdAdjacentServedFilter is primarily a repair/reorder mechanism, not a removal filter -- it never drops an organic post and drops an ad only as a last resort
claim: home-mixer/filters/ad_adjacent_served_filter.rs's filter() (L46-131) finds each ad adjacent to a previously-served post (`first_served_adjacency`) and attempts `find_swap_in_candidate` -- a search outward from the ad (near side first, then far side) for an eligible non-served, non-ad-adjacent, brand-safety-compatible post to swap into that neighboring slot (`insert_eligible_neighbour`). Only when no eligible swap candidate exists anywhere in the candidate list does the filter fall back to removing the ad itself (`removed.push(items.remove(ad_idx))`, L90-92); its own unit tests assert this explicitly ("fallback must never drop an organic post", "no organic dropped"). The filter's name ("served filter") describes only the fallback path, not its primary reorder-first behavior.

title: TopicIdsFilter's excluded-topics mode fails closed: candidates with no topic-classification data are removed, not kept
claim: home-mixer/filters/topic_ids_filter.rs's exclusion branch (L93-99, reached whenever `query.has_excluded_topics()`) partitions on `match &c.filtered_topic_ids { Some(candidate_topics) if !candidate_topics.is_empty() => !candidate_topics.iter().any(|tid| excluded_expanded.contains(tid)), _ => false }`. title: DedupConversationFilter and InvalidConversationModuleFilter are two structurally distinct conversation-collapsing mechanisms on different pipelines with similarly-scoped names
claim: home-mixer/filters/dedup_conversation_filter.rs's DedupConversationFilter runs as a PhoenixCandidatePipeline post_selection_filter (home-mixer/candidate_pipeline/phoenix_candidate_pipeline.rs L431) on the already-selected top-K set, keeping only the single highest-`score` candidate per `conversation_id` (= min of `ancestors`, or the candidate's own tweet id). home-mixer/filters/invalid_conversation_module_filter.rs's InvalidConversationModuleFilter delegates entirely to home-mixer/util/conversation_grouping.rs::select_conversation_modules, which runs as a FollowingCandidatePipeline pre-selection filter (home-mixer/candidate_pipeline/following_candidate_pipeline.rs L184-185) on unranked reverse-chron candidates, and instead keeps exactly one "focal" (deepest/max-tweet-id) reply per reply-thread root plus that reply's now-non-redundant ancestors, dropping shallower replies in the same thread and retweets of now-dropped roots. Both operate on "conversation"/reply-thread grouping and both reduce a thread to one representative item, but use different grouping keys, different pipelines, different selection criteria (highest score vs. deepest/focal reply), and run at different pipeline stages (post-selection vs. pre-selection).
